text.text: A team member is not meeting expected standards of work output, quality, or behavior. Very manageable when handled with clear documentation and consistent communication.

• An employee who consistently missed quarterly targets despite coaching conversations over three months.
• A team member whose work quality dropped since returning from a leave of absence.
• Someone who used to be a strong performer but has been disengaged and error-prone for six weeks.
• An employee who repeatedly submits reports late after multiple reminders.
• A customer-facing employee receiving escalating complaints about attitude or responsiveness.
• A team member who stops contributing in meetings and misses collaborative deadlines.
• An employee whose output volume dropped significantly without a clear explanation.
• Someone who was coached verbally twice and is now making the same errors again.
Gather and preserve these records as you work through the check.

1. Send a follow-up email after every coaching conversation summarizing what was discussed and what is expected.
2. Use a simple log: date, what you observed, what you said, how the employee responded.
3. Save any examples of substandard work — reports, emails, error logs — as attachments.
4. Document goals in writing before any review period begins so expectations are clear.
5. Note any explanation the employee gave and whether it was substantiated.

elements.text: You can attach files and links securely from the completed assessment before submitting it to HR.

text.text: Watch for: Performance issues that began after an accommodation request, leave, or protected disclosure create legal exposure and must be handled carefully.
Contact HR: If you are unsure whether the performance issue is connected to a medical condition, leave, or a recent complaint — stop and contact HR before doing anything else.
